_comment: Radiance x0 patch-16 MULTI-GPU pipeline-parallel LoRA fine-tune, weights RESIDENT. See radiance/train.py. The 9.5B model is diced into one chunk per block and the chunks are split across GPUs; only activations cross PCIe, so no NVLink is needed. Stage weights stay on their GPU — if they do not fit, switch parallelism to 'pipeline-offload'.
_comment_topology: parallelism 'pipeline' = N GPUs, resident weights. chunks_per_stage overrides the automatic split (which balances stages by WEIGHT BYTES, not chunk count — the embed chunk carries the ~603M Approximator and a double chunk weighs 2.7x a single chunk). Must sum to the number of chunks: 7 + ceil(19/bpc) + ceil(38/bpc), i.e. 64 at bpc 1.
_comment_last_stage: WATCH THE LAST STAGE. The byte-balancer sees the NeRF head as ~604M of weight but cannot see that its ACTIVATIONS are the largest in the model: each NerfGLUBlock materializes [B*N, 49152] of hypernetwork-generated weights (1.6 GB bf16 at 1024px batch 4). If anything OOMs it is the last stage, and the fix is a manual chunks_per_stage that gives it fewer chunks.
_comment_chunks: blocks_per_chunk only sets the dicing granularity here; nothing streams. grad_ckpt wraps each block in torch.utils.checkpoint (valid ONLY with resident stages) — and each NerfGLUBlock is its own checkpoint unit, which is where it pays off most.
_comment_batch: batch_size is PER MICROBATCH; effective batch = batch_size * n_microbatches.
_comment_ckpt: Path to the Radiance x0 patch-16 base weights (safetensors, native flow keys, 659 tensors). See checkpoints/README.md.
_comment_mode: mode='lora': LoRA adapters on all nn.Linear + unfrozen RMSNorm scales, whole model bf16.
